passage.title: 'Climb the Next Step', a teacher-written model speech for TGA
paras: When I was your age, I failed my first reading test. Not once: twice. I remember the red pen and the long walk home. My grandmother did not tell me I was clever. She said, 'Tomorrow, read one page more than today.' So I did. One page became ten; ten became a book; a book became a love of reading that has never left me. You will fall. You will be tired. You will want to stop. Do not stop. Climb the next step.

keywords.def: the art of speaking or writing to persuade or inspire
the people a text is for
a short personal story used to make a point
speaking straight to the listener with 'you'

questions.q: Who is the audience and what is the purpose?
questions.a: Year 7 pupils in an assembly; to inspire them to keep going when learning is hard.

questions.q: Find the image the speech shares with Mother to Son
Core: in the portal response box, write a PEEDL paragraph: 'Compare how the speech and the poem encourage perseverance.' Starter: 'Both texts encourage perseverance by...'
questions.a: A PEEDL paragraph: both use climbing and personal experience; the speech uses anecdote and the rule of three, the poem an extended metaphor and a mother's voice.

questions.q: Extend: write a fourth line for the rule of three that keeps the pattern
Stretch: which text inspires you more, and why?
questions.a: A reasoned choice referring to methods (anecdote, metaphor, voice).

questions.q: Why does the speaker begin with a story about failing?
options: to show the audience that struggle is normal and can be overcome
questions.a: B) to show the audience that struggle is normal and can be overcome. An anecdote of failure builds trust and hope.

questions.q: Answer the ponder: how do speakers inspire people?
questions.a: For example: by sharing their own struggle and ending with a clear call to action.
